result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Comparison.n]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: The number of test units (aligned rows). twitter-card: title: >- [Comparison.n]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: The number of test units (aligned rows). title: >- [Comparison.n]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: The number of test units (aligned rows). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The number of test units (aligned rows). ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [Comparison.n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} A comparison aligns the rows of the two tables and gives each aligned row one status (see the *Test Units and Row Statuses* section of [`compare()`](`pointblank.compare`)). `n` is the total, so it's always the sum of the values in [`status_counts`](`pointblank.Comparison.status_counts`) and of [`n_passed`](`pointblank.Comparison.n_passed`) and [`n_failed`](`pointblank.Comparison.n_failed`). It's the denominator to use for any fraction of rows that pass or fail. `n` isn't the row count of either table. A row that's in both tables counts once, rows in only one table count once each, and a duplicated key counts as many units as the larger of its two occurrence counts. The row counts of the two tables are available as `n_source_rows` and `n_target_rows`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} These two tables of weather station readings have four rows each, but only three stations in common. ::: {#ac318043 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl readings_v1 = pl.DataFrame( {"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"], "temp": [12.1, 14.0, 9.8, 11.2]} ) readings_v2 = pl.DataFrame( {"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S5"], "temp": [12.1, 14.3, 9.8, 8.0]} ) comparison = pb.compare(readings_v1, readings_v2, keys="station") comparison.n, comparison.n_source_rows, comparison.n_target_rows ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (5, 4, 4) ``` ::: ::: There are five test units: the three shared stations, `S4` (only in the source), and `S5` (only in the target). Dividing by `n` gives the fraction of rows that failed: ::: {#4cadbadf .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} comparison.n_failed / comparison.n ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 0.6 ``` ::: ::: Three of the five units failed: `S2` changed, `S4` is missing, and `S5` is extra.
